name: Ajogun, Ajun
body:
ARUN
CR 10

This sinister, black-robed figure has the face of a golden skull and elaborate gold necklaces round its neck. Its dark, ashen-gray hands grip a tall staff surmounted with feathers and a human skull.

XP 25,600
NE Medium outsider (ajogun, evil, extraplanar)
Init +3; Senses darkvision 60 ft., master of contagion; Perception +20
Aura pestilence (60 ft., DC 21)

DEFENSE

AC 22, touch 19, flat-footed 19 (+3 armor, +3 Dex, +6 profane)
hp 175 (13d10+104)
Fort +15, Ref +7, Will +14
Defensive Abilities indulge in suffering, shadowy dissipation; Immune compulsion, disease, exhausted, fatigued, fear, poison; SR 21

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee quarterstaff +17/+12/+7 (1d6+5 plus plague staff)
Special Attacks exacerbate disease, plague staff
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 13th; concentration +18)

At Will—blindness/deafness (DC 17), dimension door, ray of enfeeblement (DC 16), ray of sickening (DC 16)
3/day—cloudkill (DC 20), vampiric touch
1/day—blasphemy (DC 22)

STATISTICS

Str 14, Dex 16, Con 24, Int 14, Wis 18, Cha 20
Base Atk +13; CMB +15; CMD 34
Feats Deceitful, Iron Will, Persuasive, Quicken Spell-Like Ability (blindness/deafness), Skill Focus (Stealth), Stealthy, Toughness
Skills Bluff +25, Diplomacy +7, Disguise +22, Escape Artist +5, Intimidate +22, Knowledge (nature) +15, Perception +20, Perform (oratory) +18, Sense Motive +20, Stealth +29
Languages Abyssal, Common

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Disease (Ex)

The creature’s body is unable to properly absorb water; it suffers as its skin becomes dried and crackled like ancient parchment and its muscles shrink from dehydration. In a desperate attempt to rehydrate themselves, infected creatures must succeed at a DC 21 Will Save the first time each day they see a body of water large enough to submerge themselves in or will be compelled to jump in the water immediately. Any body of water that an infected creature submerges themselves in for more than 5 minutes is considered infected as well and will spread the disease through contact until no infected creature has been in it for at least a week.

Type disease, contact; save Fortitude DC 21; onset 1d4 days; frequency 1/day; Effect 1d4 Con Damage and 1d4 Dex Damage and target is fatigued; cure 2 consecutive saves.

Exacerbate Disease (Su)

When a creature is hit by any of an arun’s attacks or fails a save against an arun’s abilities, all magical contagions on the target immediately progress as if a whole day had passed, and the creature has a -4 penalty on saving throws against the disease’s progression.

Indulge in Suffering (Su)

When at least 1 creature within 100 feet is afflicted by Walking Ossification, an arun gets fast healing 5. When at least 2 creatures within 100 feet afflicted by Walking Ossification, an arun gains a +2 profane bonus to saving throws and fast healing 10 instead.

Master of Contagions (Ex)

An arun knows the location of all creatures within 1 mile that are afflicted with any form of disease or magical contagion, as well as what disease they are afflicted with and how many Hit Dice they have. While within 1 mile of an arun, diseases can only be healed with magic. In addition, they are able to extend their immunity to any diseases and poisons to any creatures of their choice within that range, usually other ajogun they are working with.

Pestilence Aura (Su)

Any creatures of an arun’s choice within the aura that are not undead or constructs must pass a DC 21 Fort Save or be afflicted with Walking Ossification and an arun can make symptoms manifest immediately instead of waiting 1d4 days if it so chooses. If it does not, the symptoms manifest in the normal timeline. Targets that pass the save are immune to this ability for 24 hours (but not the magical contagion itself, if they already have it or touch an infected creature or body of water).

Plague Staff (Su)

In an arun’s hands, any quarterstaff gains a +2 enhancement bonus and deals an additional 2d8 acid damage. In addition, the target is immediately exposed to walking ossification.

Shadowy Dissipation (Su)

Once every 1d4 minutes, when an arun uses its dimension door spell-like ability or is hit by an attack, it can choose to become invisible as though it had just cast invisibility.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary or procession (1 arun plus 3-6 other evil creatures)
Treasure standard

Ajun are harbingers of disease and death, preparing mortal bodies for harvest by the lord of the ajogun, Iku. They appear as men dressed in black finery, decked in head to toe with elaborate ornamentation that always include a golden skull mask, necklaces of gold and cowrie shells, and golden bracelets. In addition, each bears a skull-tipped staff that causes heinous disease with a single touch.

Lacking combat prowess, ajun prefer to feast on the suffering and misery brought about by the disease they inflict. Local apothecaries and healers will see rashes of disease that no potions or magics seem to be able to cure; entire settlements will come down with unusually resistant diseases and slowly wither and decay as the entire population falls too sick to be able to maintain even basic daily tasks.

Because they enjoy feeding on the suffering from disease, ajun tend to work with other ajogun, but usually will not work with another ajun. When traveling, the ajun and their traveling companions might be mistaken for a clergy or medicine man coming to heal an afflicted town but make no mistake… they are there to pave the way for Iku’s arrival.
